papers.title: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms
papers.abstract: We present new information-theoretic protocols for $s$-server, doubly-efficient private information retrieval (PIR) in sublinear server time and one extra bit of space on the servers, for every constant $s \geq 2$. On an $n$-bit database, each of the $s$ PIR servers first builds and stores a preprocessing data structure consisting of $n+1$ bits (which is unique to each server, and after which the server may discard the original database). Then, each server answers a PIR query in time $T_s(n)$, by reading at most $T_s$ bits of its data structure and sending them to the user. In the two server setting ($s=2$), our PIR protocols achieve $T_2 = n^{0.82}$, matching the server time of the state-of-the-art schemes of Henzinger and Ragavan (EUROCRYPT 2026) while shrinking their storage from $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ to $n+1$ bits. With $s \geq 3$ servers, our PIR protocols retain the $n+1$ bits of storage and additionally improve on the server time of all prior information-theoretic $s$-server schemes with $n^{1+o(1)}$ storage: for example, achieving $T_3 = n^{0.74}$ and $T_{10} = n^{0.61}$ (previously $n^{0.79}$ and $n^{0.75}$). Asymptotically, as the server count $s$ grows, we shrink the number of servers required to achieve a given server-work exponent from $s^{3.9}$ to $s$. Our results draw inspiration from matching-vector techniques (Efremenko, STOC 2009), which we generalize to handle degree-two computations in the exponent. Using this generalization, we build doubly-efficient PIR from the new intermediate abstraction of Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions. Then, we construct such Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions via a connection to modular forms and complex analysis: if a Fourier-sparse cone-delta function does not exist, then there exists a modular form which has too many roots, contradicting the valence formula.

papers.title: The Maximum Number of Sets for 12 Cards is 14
papers.abstract: We analyze a mathematical property of the popular card game SET. We present a revised geometric and computer-assisted proof that the maximum number of sets for 12 cards is 14 using finite field geometry, combinatorics, and graph theory. We present several computer algorithms for finding or approximating the maximum number of sets. We show a complete computer proof that iterates over all possible board configurations. We use this method to compute the maximum number of sets with 4 properties for a small number of cards, but it is generally too inefficient. With this method, we compute the maximum number of sets for 3 properties for all possible numbers of cards. Finally, we compare this to an existing approximation algorithm for finding maximal sets.

papers.title: Certified finite-precision readout for $p$-adic kernel aggregation
papers.abstract: In non-archimedean numerical analysis, a verified $p$-adic approximation can determine an absolute value, and hence downstream probabilistic rankings and classification decisions, with mathematical exactness long before the underlying number is fully resolved. We turn this observation into rigorous finite-precision certificates for norm-based readouts of amplitude families. For a common error radius, a nonempty resolved set already fixes every exact maximizer, ties included, at the sharp integer absolute precision $v_*+1$, and conditioning on that set yields an exact total-variation identity separating unresolved $p$-adic mass from real rounding error. For aggregates of $p$-adic exponentials, we give a centered-moment certificate with an explicit remainder bound: on rational data it runs in exact rational arithmetic without individual exponential evaluations, attains its minimal bound at an active phase, and resolves every nonzero aggregate at high order; we also obtain an aggregate perturbation bound free of summand-count factors. For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.

papers.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
papers.abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $\chi$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

papers.title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
papers.abstract: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{\deg_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.

papers.title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=\eta^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $\eta\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $\eta^{q^n}=-\eta$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $\delta=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-\delta)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $\delta=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.

papers.title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
papers.abstract: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.

papers.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
papers.abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

papers.title: $(G,\mu)$-Windows and Deformations of $(G,\mu)$-Displays
papers.abstract: Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let $\mu$ be a cocharacter of $G_{W(k_0)}$ such that the set of $\mu$-weights of $\Lie G$ is a subset of $\{-1,0,1,2,\dots\}$. We prove that the groupoid of adjoint nilpotent $(G,\mu)$-displays as in \cite[Definition 1.0.1]{pappas}, \cite{lau2} and \cite[Definition 3.16]{E7} is equivalent to the groupoid of $(G,\mu)$-windows, which are the generalizations of windows as in \cite[Definition 5.1]{langer2} and \cite[Definition 3.3.1]{E7}.

papers.title: On the Drinfeld formal group
papers.abstract: We identify Drinfeld's formal group on the prismatization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a formal group arising from homotopy theory, given locally by the Quillen formal group of a decompleted variant of topological periodic cyclic homology. We also prove that this formal group extends to the syntomization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$, and that it admits a certain algebraization conjectured by Drinfeld.

papers.title: Torsion of elliptic curves over quartic number fields with rational $j$-invariant
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve defined over a quartic extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with $j(E)\in\mathbb{Q}$. We classify the possible group structures of $E(K)_{\mathrm{tors}}$, concluding that the only additional possibilities, besides those occuring over quartic fields by base change from elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$, are $\mathbb{Z}/17\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/21\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences
papers.abstract: We determine the exact completeness threshold for standard positive linear recurrence sequences whose coefficient lists consist of leading units, followed by zeros and a final positive coefficient. Using the generating function of Brown's gaps, we prove a necessary and sufficient condition for completeness, including the boundary case in which the critical gap vanishes. We further establish strict monotonicity of the unrounded threshold in the number of leading units, thereby resolving the corresponding leading-unit monotonicity conjecture.

papers.title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
papers.abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.

papers.title: A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
papers.abstract: For every nonempty finite set $S$ of $N$ positive integers we prove $-\min_{x\in\mathbb{T}}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2\pi sx)\gg (N/\log(2N))^{1/4}$. The proof uses a reversible phase kernel whose one-step and two-step laws are close in total variation. Comparison of rows and a height cutoff produce a partition into pieces of bounded mean. A Fourier rounding estimate then forces many additive triples to cross the partition. Two choices of phase density yield bounds in terms of negative mass and an exact conditional-pair defect, respectively. A logarithmic refinement gives a log-free bound at low triple density. At fixed positive triple density the log-free bound is a corollary of known boundary estimates. We give a separate spectral proof using an integer difference count and a theorem of Yip.

papers.title: A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
papers.abstract: The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained. An example of applying the criterion to a series whose Cantorval property was previously unknown is given. A more general object of study of topological properties is the set of numbers whose representations in a numerical system with a natural base and a redundant alphabet are subject to restrictions on the use of digits. It is for this object that the above statements are proved.

papers.title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
papers.abstract: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.

papers.title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
papers.abstract: We study the $\theta$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+\delta}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $\theta$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower $\theta$-intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for $\theta$ in an interval.

papers.title: Avoiding short progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory II
papers.abstract:
Recently, Currier, Moore, and Yip developed a general framework for constructing colorings avoiding prescribed monochromatic arithmetic progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Writing $\ell_m$ for an $m$-term arithmetic progression with unit spacing, they proved $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\ell_{20})$ and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{6889})$ for every $\alpha>0$. We refine and simplify their framework, proving $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{22})$ for every $\alpha>0$. We further establish $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{21})$ except possibly for four values of $\alpha^2$, and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{17})$ for all but finitely many $\alpha>0$. Our approach also recovers several earlier results and avoids some technical arguments used in previous works.

papers.title: Orbits along primes in totally minimal systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.

papers.title: A singular homeomorphism between Pierce expansions and continued fraction expansions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the map $\Theta$ which sends each $x\in[0,1]$ to the number whose continued fraction digits are the first Pierce expansion digit of $x$ and the gaps between two consecutive Pierce expansion digits of $x$. We investigate the regularity of $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$, including the optimal H\"older exponent of $\Theta^{-1}$, and the local and Hausdorff dimensions of the push-forwards of the Lebesgue measure under $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$. We also study the differentiability of $\Theta$ at rational and irrational points, and calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the set of points at which $\Theta$ has an infinite derivative.

papers.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
papers.abstract: Let $\lambda$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_\lambda(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n)e^{2\pi i n\alpha}\right|\,d\alpha. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_{\lambda}(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]

papers.title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
papers.abstract: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bella\"iche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$.

papers.title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
papers.abstract: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.

papers.title: Geometry of multidimensional Farey summation algorithm and frieze patterns
papers.abstract: In this paper we develop a new geometric approach to subtractive continued fraction algorithms in high dimensions. We adapt a version of Farey summation to the geometric techniques proposed by F. Klein in 1895. More specifically we introduce Farey polyhedra and their sails that generalise respectively Klein polyhedra and their sails, and show similar duality properties of the Farey sail integer invariants. The construction of Farey sails is based on the multidimensional generalisation of the Farey tessellation provided by a modification of the continued fraction algorithm introduced by R. W. J. Meester. We classify Farey polyhedra in the combinatorial terms of prismatic diagrams. Prismatic diagrams extend boat polygons introduced by S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko in the two-dimensional case. As one of the applications of the new theory we get a multidimensional version of Conway-Coxeter frieze patterns. We show that multidimensional frieze patterns satisfy generalised Ptolemy relations.

papers.title: Orthogonality of non-pretentious functions to polynomials over Function Fields
papers.abstract: We prove that non-pretentious multiplicative functions are orthogonal to polynomials over function fields (up to characteristic conditions).

papers.title: Discovering hypergeometric series with harmonic numbers via Wilf-Zeilberger seeds
papers.abstract: By extracting coefficients from Wilf-Zeilberger pairs with respect to auxiliary parameters, we discover many nontrivial hypergeometric series involving harmonic numbers. In particular, we obtain a rapidly convergent series for the depth-two multiple zeta value $\zeta(5,3)$, which appears to be the first result of its kind in the literature. We also investigate the Hilbert series attached to a WZ-seed and conjecture that it admits a remarkably simple form, suggesting the presence of an underlying graded-algebra structure associated with WZ-seeds.

papers.title: A criterion for weighted uniform distribution along functions from a Hardy field
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Boshernitzan states that if $f$ is a function which belongs to a Hardy field and which satisfies $|f(x)|\prec x^{\ell}$ for some $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, then the sequence $(f(n))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly distributed modulo 1 if and only if $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{|f(x)-p(x)|}{\log(x)} = \infty$ for all $p(x)\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. We provide a new proof of this result using methods from summability theory and we extend Boshernitzan's criterion by obtaining necessary and sufficient conditions for $f$ to be uniformly distributed modulo 1 with respect to a broad class of weighted averages. As an application of our results, we show that for the function $f(x) = x^{3/2}$ and for any $(a,b)\subset [0,1]$, and all sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an $n\in [N-N^{\frac{1}{4}},N]$ such that $f(n)\mod 1\in (a,b)$.

papers.title: Beyond Mock Modularity: Elliptic Corrections for Higher Dyson Ranks
papers.abstract: When $m = 1$, the Dyson rank generating function is a classical bridge between partition theory, Ramanujan's mock theta functions, and the theory of harmonic Maass forms and nonholomorphic Jacobi forms. The rank is a statistic on partitions, and the higher Dyson systems, for $m \geq 2$, are a natural multivariable refinement of it, combining $m$ graded rank contributions. Unlike the classical case, these higher systems are not expected to fit the mock-modular framework, which raises the question of what analytic structure governs them. We show that their root-of-unity specializations carry a hidden elliptic structure. For $m\ge2$, the primitive $(2m+1)$st-root specialization of their generating function leads to a product deformation whose associated seed satisfies a finite $q$-difference recurrence with an explicit polynomial defect. Using bilateral periodization we construct a meromorphic lift satisfying a twisted index-$m$ elliptic transformation law, with at most simple poles on a prescribed lattice orbit. The poles can be removed by subtracting an explicit multiple of an Appell--Lerch kernel and a specified translation removes the twist. The resulting holomorphic finite parts admit a finite theta decomposition. These results grew out of a human--AI collaboration, and the key new formulas were formalized and machine-verified in Lean/Mathlib by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Sidon sets with $\Delta$-separated sumsets in additive number theory
papers.abstract: The set $A$ is a $B_h$-set if every element of the sumset $hA$ has a unique representation as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. A $B_2$-set is also called a Sidon set. A $B_{h,\Delta}$-set is a $B_h$-set $A$ whose sumset $hA$ is $\Delta$-separated, that is, $|x-x'| \geq \Delta$ for all $x,x' \in hA$ with $x\neq x'$. Upper and lower bounds are obtained for the cardinality of the largest $B_{2,\Delta}$-sets contained in $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$, that is, sets $A \subseteq \{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ such that, if $a,b,c,d \in A$ and $\{a,b\} \neq \{c,d\}$, then $|(a+b)-(c+d)| \geq \Delta$.

papers.title: A recursion relation for the coefficients of Swinnerton-Dyer type polynomials
papers.abstract: We study a family of polynomials that are very closely related to the Swinnerton-Dyer polynomials. As main result, we determine a recursion relation for the coefficients of this family of polynomials. We briefly explain our own and others' interest in this family of polynomials.
